solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Loot's bound to excite British swimmer

indicators.note: something bound is tied around, so the loot wraps round what follows it

blocks.note: to tickle someone is to excite or amuse them
standard abbreviation
sack as in plunder, what an army takes from a captured town

explanation.surface: A thief's haul is sure to thrill some British swimmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' reads as certain to, but it means tied around: the loot encloses the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The stickleback is a small spiny freshwater fish, and any fish counts as a swimmer in crosswords.

clue.text: Case flung about with feet in British infant school?

indicators.note: things flung about land in a jumble, so the letters are reordered
in a down entry the foot of each word is its last letter

blocks.note: taken as written
the final letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A child's bag hurled around the playground of a British infant school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' is used twice: as the definition and as part of the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A satchel is a shoulder bag for carrying school books, a kind of carrying case.

clue.text: Patriarch funds promotion of accountant

indicators.note: promotion moves things upward, and in a down entry going up means reading backwards

blocks.note: an ISA is an Individual Savings Account, a British tax-free savings fund
chartered accountant

explanation.surface: A senior figure finances an accountant's promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac, son of Abraham and father of Jacob, is one of the three biblical patriarchs.

clue.text: Pot poured out to rouse bird

indicators.note: words poured out are spoken, so the spelling follows the sound and not the usual form

blocks.note: a kitty is a shared pot of money
to rouse someone is to wake them

explanation.surface: Tipping a pot out to wake a sleeping bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The kittiwake is a small gull of the North Atlantic named for its call.

clue.text: Story elevating European and other people

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising a letter lifts it from the bottom to the top of the word

blocks.note: a tale is a story
names the letter E that is moved

explanation.surface: A tale that celebrates a European and others.
explanation.walkthrough: The final E of TALE moves to the top.
explanation.definitionFit: Et al is Latin shorthand for et alii, used to mean and others in lists of names.

clue.text: Head of army breaking ranks when somewhere in US

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
breaking ranks means falling out of order, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the first letter of this word
mixed together with the letter from army
as means when, as in as I left

explanation.surface: An army officer breaking formation while stationed somewhere in America.
explanation.definitionFit: Arkansas is a state in the southern United States, so it is one place in the US.

clue.text: Artist style boosted by gap in market

indicators.note: a boost lifts something, and in a down entry going up means reading backwards
leaving a gap in the word empties its middle, keeping only the outside letters

blocks.note: ilk means kind or type, as in of that ilk
the first and last letters of this word

explanation.surface: An artist whose style found a gap in the art market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gap in market' sounds like a business opportunity, but it removes the inside of market.
explanation.definitionFit: Gustav Klimt was the Austrian painter of The Kiss, a leading Vienna Secession artist.

clue.text: Dig around green, reviewing ancient period

indicators.note: re-viewing suggests looking back, so the word for green is read backwards
the word for dig goes round the outside of the other piece

blocks.note: to mine is to dig
eco means environmentally green

explanation.surface: An archaeologist digging around a village green while reviewing an ancient period.
explanation.definitionFit: The Miocene is a geological epoch of the Neogene, roughly 23 to 5 million years ago.

clue.text: Note unusual tracks Manilow sung – in this voice?

indicators.note: something sung is heard rather than seen, so the name goes in by its sound
unusual means out of the normal order, so the letters are rearranged
to track something is to follow behind it, so the note comes after the name

blocks.note: Barry Manilow, the American pop singer
these four letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A singer's unusual notes on tracks crooned by Barry Manilow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tracks' looks like songs on an album but means follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Baritone is the male singing voice between bass and tenor, roughly the range Manilow sings in.

clue.text: Item on breakfast table, perhaps rolled oats, eaten by dog

indicators.note: rolled oats are only one possible form, so the oats may be rolled into another order
what is eaten goes inside the eater, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: these four letters are mixed
to dog someone is to follow or track them

explanation.surface: A breakfast table holding porridge oats being wolfed by the family dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog' is a verb here, meaning follow, not the pet.
explanation.definitionFit: A toast rack is the little stand that holds slices of toast upright at the breakfast table.

clue.text: State aid distributed by hand outs, initially

indicators.note: things distributed are spread about, so the letters are scattered into a fresh order
initially points at the opening letter of each of the words before it

blocks.note: these three letters are mixed
the first letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Government relief being handed out to people in need.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hand outs' reads like handouts, the charity, but it is two words whose first letters are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is one of the fifty states of the USA, in the north-west of the country.

clue.text: Feverish man, cold, twitching

blocks.note: a man is a he
C for cold, as on a tap
a tic is an involuntary twitching

explanation.surface: A sick man shivering with cold and twitching in a fever.
explanation.definitionFit: Hectic originally described the flushed, feverish state of consumption before it came to mean frantic.

clue.text: Fast train disrupted by frost

indicators.note: a disrupted service is thrown into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: these five letters are mixed
frost is a thin covering of ice

explanation.surface: An express train held up by frost on the line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' looks like an adjective for the train, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In a trice means in an instant, very quickly, so it can stand for fast used as an adverb.

clue.text: Archaic language disgusted daily newspaper's chief

indicators.note: read as dis-gusted, a word blown apart, so its letters are scrambled
the chief letter of a word is its leading one

blocks.note: these five letters are mixed
the first letter of this word

explanation.surface: An editor appalled by the outdated language in the daily paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Lydian was the extinct Anatolian tongue spoken in ancient Lydia, the kingdom of Croesus.

clue.text: Air currents cause diversion on board

blocks.note: first meaning: cold flows of air through a room
second meaning: a board game played for amusement, called checkers in the US

explanation.surface: Breezes on a ship's deck causing a change of course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' suggests a ship, but it means on a game board.
explanation.definitionFit: Draughts are chilly airflows indoors, and also the British name for the game Americans call checkers.

clue.text: Ballet movement, somewhere in South America, screened by digital TV

indicators.note: something screened is shielded on both sides, so the place sits within the television service

blocks.note: cable is a digital television service
Rio de Janeiro in Brazil

explanation.surface: A ballet performed in Brazil, shown on a digital television channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screened' suggests broadcasting, but here it means hidden behind, so the city is enclosed.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabriole is a leap in which a dancer beats one leg against the other in mid-air.

clue.text: Disgraced broadcaster craftily won over the quaint English town

indicators.note: something done craftily is twisted cunningly, so these letters are rearranged
in a down entry one piece placed over another simply comes before it

blocks.note: Jonathan Ross, suspended by the BBC in 2008 over prank phone calls
these three letters are mixed
ye is a mock-old form of the, as in Ye Olde Shoppe

explanation.surface: A shamed presenter cunningly wins over a picturesque English market town.
explanation.walkthrough: Jonathan Ross was a British TV and radio host suspended in the 2008 Sachsgate scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ross-on-Wye is a market town in Herefordshire, England, standing on the River Wye.

clue.text: Split gutted increasingly odd musician?

indicators.note: a gutted fish has had its insides taken out, so only the outer letters of the word stay

blocks.note: taken as written
rum is British for odd, so rummer means odder

explanation.surface: A band falling apart as its gutted members grow ever stranger.
explanation.walkthrough: Rum is old British slang for strange. 'Gutted' looks like dismayed, but it empties the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A strummer is someone who strums a guitar, so a musician by definition of the question mark.

clue.text: Attempt to obtain adult underwear for burlesque

indicators.note: to obtain is to take in and hold, so the attempt holds what follows within it

blocks.note: a try is an attempt
A for adult, the old film certificate
a vest is an undershirt in Britain

explanation.surface: Trying to buy grown-up lingerie for a saucy stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a vest is an undershirt worn beneath a shirt, not a waistcoat.
explanation.definitionFit: A travesty is a grotesque mockery or parody of something serious, exactly what a burlesque performance offers.

clue.text: Company meeting as yet to be fixed – is it appointed by 9?

indicators.note: something still to be fixed is not yet in order, so the letters await arranging

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
taken as written

explanation.surface: A company meeting whose agenda and appointments are still undecided.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 refers to the answer at 9 across, TOAST RACK; 'appointed' plays on positions in a company.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea cosy is a padded cover that keeps the teapot warm, set on the breakfast table beside the toast rack.

clue.text: Value two letters written about Terence when evacuated

indicators.note: an evacuated name has had its insides emptied, leaving only its two outer letters
letters written about something are set around it on either side

blocks.note: the letter S spelt out as a word
the first and last letters of this name
the letter M spelt out as a word

explanation.surface: Valuing a pair of letters a correspondent sent to someone named Terence.
explanation.walkthrough: The two letters are ES and EM, the spelt-out names of S and M, placed either side of TE.
explanation.definitionFit: To esteem something is to value it highly or hold it in high regard.

clue.text: Fellowship disciple enthralled by religious icon

indicators.note: someone enthralled is held captive, so this piece is held inside the other

blocks.note: the Virgin Mary
a disciple is a son of his master in the figurative sense

explanation.surface: A follower captivated by a holy image of the Madonna.
explanation.definitionFit: Masonry here means freemasonry, the brotherhood of masons, a society bound by fellowship.

clue.text: Emperor, right away, foretells time allied to America

indicators.note: away means sent off, so the letter for right is removed from the word for foretells

blocks.note: to augur is to foretell
standard abbreviation
the United States

explanation.surface: A Roman ruler predicting, straight away, a future alliance with America.
explanation.walkthrough: AUGURS loses its R (right) to leave AUGUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Augustus was the first Roman emperor, the adopted heir of Julius Caesar.

clue.text: Excessive energy impedes stride

indicators.note: something that impedes stands in the way, so it sits in the middle of the other word

blocks.note: a stride is a step
standard abbreviation in physics

explanation.surface: Too much effort holds back a runner's stride.
explanation.definitionFit: Steep is informal for unreasonably high, as in a steep price, so excessive in amount.

clue.text: Ice hockey team squeezes into some foreign cinema

indicators.note: foreign suggests something strange and unfamiliar, so these letters appear in an unfamiliar order
what squeezes into something ends up inside it

blocks.note: these four letters are mixed
an ice hockey side has six players, VI in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A hockey team crowding into a little foreign picture house.
explanation.walkthrough: VI goes inside the mixed letters of some.
explanation.definitionFit: The movies is an informal name for cinema as an art form or entertainment.

clue.text: Tongue skimmed by dentist's latest piece of metal

indicators.note: skimming takes off the top layer, and in a down entry the top is the first letter
the latest letter of a word is its final one

blocks.note: lingo is slang for a language or tongue
the final letter of this word

explanation.surface: A dentist's latest metal filling grazing the patient's tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tongue' is the language sense, not the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingot is a block of cast metal, typically gold or silver, shaped like a brick.

clue.text: Georgia repeatedly out to lunch

indicators.note: repeatedly tells us the abbreviation appears twice in succession

blocks.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state
the same abbreviation again

explanation.surface: A Georgian who keeps being out at lunchtime.
explanation.definitionFit: Out to lunch is slang for crazy or not all there, which is what gaga means informally.

clue.text: Extravagant part of accoutrement

indicators.note: the answer is only a portion of the following word, sitting inside it

blocks.note: found inside this word

explanation.surface: A showy, over-the-top piece of costume kit.
explanation.definitionFit: Outre, from French, means unconventional or bizarre, beyond the bounds of the usual.

clue.text: Margaret receives ruling to sever foot on ambulance

indicators.note: foot gives F, and severing it cuts that letter off the front of the ruling
whoever receives something holds it, so the ruling sits within the name

blocks.note: Meg is a pet form of Margaret
a fatwa is a ruling on Islamic law
taken as written

explanation.surface: Margaret is handed a court order to amputate a foot, ending up in an ambulance.
explanation.walkthrough: Foot stands for its abbreviation F, which is cut away; 'on' is wordplay, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat wagon is grim slang for an ambulance or a hearse, the vehicle that collects bodies.

clue.text: For good royal chap, hospital department induced good condition

indicators.note: read as in-duced, led in, so the chain of pieces is placed inside the final one

blocks.note: Elizabeth Regina, the Queen's cipher
a chap is a man
ear, nose and throat
in good ply, an old phrase for in good shape or form

explanation.surface: A royal attendant brought into hospital and treated until he is in good shape.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, MAN and ENT go inside PLY. ER stands for Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: Permanently and for good both mean forever, without any end, as an adverbial phrase.
